standard_prerequisites.name: Cone of a morphism of dg modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cone C(f) of f : X -> Y is the dg module Y direct sum X[1] carrying the inclusion i, the projection p and the differential built from d_Y, f and the shifted d_X.
standard_prerequisites.use: The maps i_1, p_1, i_2, p_2 and the differentials of the two cones are what the constructed c must be compatible with (source lines 655-658, 672-680).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy between morphisms of dg modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: A homotopy between two morphisms of dg modules is a graded map h of degree minus one such that their difference equals d h plus h d.
standard_prerequisites.use: The homotopy h between f_2 a and b f_1 becomes the off-diagonal entry of the matrix defining c and is what makes c a morphism of dg modules (source lines 666-672).

standard_prerequisites.name: Morphism of triangles in the homotopy category
standard_prerequisites.statement: A morphism between two distinguished triangles is a triple of morphisms making the two relevant squares commute in the homotopy category.
standard_prerequisites.use: The conclusion is that the triple (a, b, c) is such a morphism (source lines 674-680).

core_obligations: Take the homotopy and define the morphism: let h : K_1 -> L_2 be a homotopy between f_2 composed with a and b composed with f_1, and define c : L_1 direct sum K_1 -> L_2 direct sum K_2 by the block matrix with entries b, h in the first row and 0, a in the second row (source lines 666-672).
Check that c is a morphism of dg modules: verify by a matrix computation that c intertwines the differentials of the two cones, which uses the homotopy identity for h (source lines 672-673).

Check the compatibility with the triangle structure: verify the two identities c composed with i_1 equals i_2 composed with b and p_2 composed with c equals a composed with p_1, and conclude that the triple (a, b, c) is a morphism of triangles in the homotopy category (source lines 674-680).

proof_roadmap.step: Take the homotopy h and define c by the block matrix with entries b, h, 0, a.
Matrix computation: c commutes with the differentials of the two cones.
Check the two identities with the cone inclusion and projection and conclude the morphism of triangles.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-functorial-cone at source lines 643-662: for a differential graded algebra A and a square of homomorphisms of dg A-modules which is commutative up to homotopy, there is a morphism c : C(f_1) -> C(f_2) that together with the given vertical maps gives a morphism of the triangles (K_1, L_1, C(f_1), f_1, i_1, p_1) and (K_2, L_2, C(f_2), f_2, i_2, p_2) in the homotopy category. The proof at source lines 664-680 is short but it is the construction that makes the cone functorial, and the construction is the substance: it takes the homotopy h between f_2 a and b f_1, defines c by the block matrix with entries b, h, 0 and a on L_1 direct sum K_1, must verify by a matrix computation that this c commutes with the differentials (which is exactly where the homotopy is used, since in the strictly commutative case the off-diagonal entry would have to vanish), and then checks the two compatibility identities with the cone's inclusion and projection. The statement records none of the matrix, and the role of the homotopy in the differential computation is the point of the argument. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
